title: How steel is made: oxygen furnaces and recycled scrap
examples: How is steel made from iron?
What is the difference between iron and steel?

explain.say: Iron straight from a blast furnace has about 4 percent carbon, which makes it hard but brittle. Steel is iron with much less carbon, usually under 1 percent, often with small amounts of other metals.

explain.say: In a basic oxygen furnace, pure oxygen is blown at supersonic speed onto molten iron. It burns the extra carbon away as gas, and the reaction is so hot that cold scrap steel is added to stop it overheating.

explain.say: An electric arc furnace melts scrap steel instead. Huge carbon electrodes are lowered in, and electric arcs hotter than 3,000 degrees Celsius melt a load of old cars, beams and cans in under an hour.

explain.say: Steel can be recycled over and over without losing its strength. Making it from scrap in an arc furnace uses much less energy and gives off far less carbon dioxide than starting from ore.

faq.q: What is the difference between iron and steel?
faq.a: Steel is iron with its carbon cut to usually under 1 percent, often with other metals added. Blast-furnace iron, with about 4 percent carbon, is brittle; steel is tough and can bend without snapping.
asks: Is steel the same as iron?

faq.q: How does a basic oxygen furnace work?
faq.a: Molten iron and some scrap are poured into a tilting vessel, and a water-cooled lance blows pure oxygen onto the iron. The oxygen burns off extra carbon and other impurities in about 20 minutes, turning the iron into steel.
asks: Tell me about the Basic oxygen furnace

faq.q: How does an electric arc furnace work?
faq.a: Scrap steel is loaded into a furnace, and three large graphite electrodes are lowered in. Huge currents jump from them to the scrap as arcs, melting it, and the steel is then refined and poured.
asks: Tell me about the Electric arc furnace

faq.a: Yes. Steel can be melted and remade again and again with no loss of quality, which is why scrap is so valuable. Magnets make it easy to pull steel out of mixed waste.

faq.q: Why is steelmaking bad for the climate?
faq.a: Most steel still starts in blast furnaces, which use coke from coal to remove oxygen from iron ore, releasing lots of carbon dioxide. Steel accounts for around 7 percent of world emissions, so recycling and hydrogen-based methods are growing.
asks: How can steel be made greener?

facts: In 2023, basic oxygen furnaces made roughly 70 percent of the world's steel and electric arc furnaces about 30 percent (worldsteel).
Steel can be recycled repeatedly without losing its properties.

quiz.say: What does the oxygen do in a basic oxygen furnace?

options.show: Burns away extra carbon from the iron
options.say: Burns away extra carbon from the iron

options.show: Adds oxygen atoms to make the steel stronger
options.say: Adds oxygen atoms to make the steel stronger

quiz.why: Oxygen reacts with the carbon dissolved in the iron, removing it as gas so the iron becomes steel.

wrong.1: The reaction gives off heat; scrap is added to cool it, not the oxygen.
wrong.2: The oxygen leaves as carbon monoxide and dioxide; it is not meant to stay in the steel.
